**9th May 2556, 1031 hours**

**Unknown planet**

"Punch it again, this time real fuckin' slow," Stan called out, his hand firmly pressing a gauge into a small outlet on a pipe manifold.

After a few seconds a soft hiss echoed through the pipes as the manifold filled up and the gauge's needle raised slowly. Once it got to the spot Stan wanted it he called out again, "woah there!" A moment later the needle weaved over the desired mark on the gauge, when it held it indicated a stable pressure.

"Out-fucking-standing baby, ya'll got it right on the money."

Jade poked her head around the intake. "Aren't you glad you took me home with you?"

"Every day and every night."

After a few hundred turns of a ratchet he closed the cover to the manifold, nodding slowly afterward; she would hold. When he was a younger man, a boy really, he learned the value of overhauling anything that flew. During those days the war was in full swing and sometimes shortcuts were taken, it wasn't *his* way but he had seen it done and didn't report it. As he ran his hand along the line the memories flooded back in, the Kriegsmark was a Waylander class and quite similar to the Brigand II bomber that he serviced way back in 2285. Who was flying it that day? Stan couldn't place his face, truthfully he wasn't even sure if "Lt. Grange" was the guy's actual name. What he could remember was the sound of the crash klaxon blaring a warning before the crippled bomber wiped eight men off the flight deck, then the fire.

That was why regular maintenance was important, some dumb shit-for-brains decides he didn't feel like taking the extra step to do it right and something as small as a control chip put in backwards gets people killed. Too bad about that bird's crew chief, a day later the guy hung himself even though he hadn't technically done anything wrong.

"Honey?"

Stan jerked out of his trance and looked at her, his mind scrambling to collect itself. "What? What's up?"

"You okay?" she laughed. "Deep thoughts?"

He shook his head with a dismissing wave. "We gotta get the intake cleaned out, check that aux line on the port thruster... Mmm, best we look all over the electrical."

They both were filthy with grease and grime, but she still stood up on her toes and gave him a peck on the lips anyway. "Old piece of junk," she sighed, glancing up at the open panels. "I'll see to the wiring, get me a diagram?"

"She ain't junk, she's just old. Like me, that's why I need a little paddin' on my girl to keep me from bustin' a hip," he said as he slapped her backside before giving it a firm squeeze.

"Ah! No no, none of that!" Jade exclaimed as she peeled away, arching her back so she could look down at the big handprint with a grin. "Well there goes sitting on anything, you ass."

They would have been forced to lose the clothes anyway, Inzili kept a neat house and wouldn't have allowed them to touch anything. Not that they would have, Stan wasn't exactly a neat freak but he didn't like a mess and Jade had been "housetrained" for the most part. That didn't stop her from cluttering up the small engineering section in the center aft portion of the ship, but she spent most her time there when she wasn't with everyone else. That didn't stop Inzili from occasionally getting annoyed, and it was one of the *few* things they ever seriously fought about.

"There's one in that trunk," he said with a pointed ratchet. When she sauntered over to it he had to laugh, the hand print oscillated with each step. "Geez, killin' me with that tight jumpsuit."

Of course the only reason why it was tight was her recent weight gain, the suit fit nicely before the pregnancy. Maybe it was the thought of knowing how he "made" her gain weight, but she seemed more attractive with it than without. As long as she didn't need to go up a size, but she would probably need to work to make that happen since she was normally quite active.

Jade pulled out the little booklet and flipped through a few pages. "Baby, we really should put in new wiring when we get a chance. I'd feel better knowing it was... I guess modern. Sorry!"

"Hah, modern. Well I reckon you do have a point, it's as old as you are," he admitted, giving her a look over. She would be twenty-seven in December, he had installed it around that time. "What would you suggest?"

"Well for the power we're good, but data? I mean some of it's the original cables, so that is like... not fast."

Back when it was new it wasn't top of the line, it was there for durability. "Yeah, I reckon y'all gotta point there. We better get back to it though."

"So like, is that a yes?"

From her tone he could tell she was in the early stages of irritation, but he didn't want to agree to anything. "Tell you what, lemme look over some stuff and I'll come up with somethin' for you. Promise."

"Baby, you better."

He took a stride toward her and caught her in an embrace. "I promise. No bullshit."

"Mmm. Mmm-mm, I'm not gonna fall for it. For once I'm really, really serious. Okay?"

"So am I!" he lied, he had totally different plans. "I promise I will get back to you with something. You'll like it."

*That* wasn't a lie, and his tone reflected it. Instead of arguing further she just gave him a parting kiss and a look, she could be intimidating when she wanted to be. No doubt when she went inside she would tell Inzili all about the exchange and probably plan some sort of ambush later on, to which he'd have to act surprised. Some might have frowned at that but they didn't understand that he enjoyed the give and take with them, somebody could insult his "manhood" all they wanted but he didn't care. Masculinity was unimportant to him, his was ironclad as far as he was concerned, when it came to doing "man shit" the loudest boasters tended to flounder and fail. He just preferred to get shit done, no fanfare, none of that. Plus they missed the bigger picture: there was no gain in revealing that he knew they conspired against him, it made staying ahead even easier.

That thought rang in his head like a bell, they hadn't tasted good and fresh meat in awhile and he knew the perfect way to diffuse their inevitable dinner-time ambush. They were "lizards" after all, Inzili was pretty much a carnivore and Jade... well, she would eat almost anything that passed the "it tastes good" test. On his way to get a rifle he thought of an immediate problem: he knew precisely jack shit about the local wildlife. That didn't stop him before, but it raised a dilemma in that he could ask or he could just slink away into a potentially lethal situation.

"I better leave a note."
